blocks.text: Mark’s opening scenes place teaching, healing, hospitality, and rejection within village life and movement between nearby settlements. This makes houses and village networks part of the setting in which Jesus’s Galilean activity unfolds, not merely background scenery. An excavation in central Nazareth has identified an early Roman-period dwelling with rock-cut storage installations and locally used pottery, supporting the picture of Nazareth as an inhabited village in this period. It does not, however, identify the synagogue in the story or a particular family home.
